minutes.headline: Water commissioners heard a draft master plan recommending a combined PFAS treatment plant at Lancaster Ave for two wells.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water Commissioners met mainly to hear a consultant present the draft master plan on PFAS treatment, well capacity and water quality. The plan recommends one plant at Lancaster Avenue treating Lancaster and Hickory Hills water, plus a separate plant at Keating, with state SRF financing and deadlines discussed. Commissioners asked questions and thanked the presenters; the only motion was to adjourn.

budget_items.topic: Combined Lancaster/Hickory Hills treatment plant with transmission main
budget_items.what_was_said: Presenter gave an all-in budget figure for the combined plant including the main across town.
Standalone plant at Keating estimated separately.
The state revolving fund offers zero percent financing and possible principal forgiveness, which helps finance these projects.
The longer looping route would cost more than the shorter route.
figures_as_heard: a little over 2.1 or 2.2 million more

budget_items.what_was_said: First-year SRF funding is capped regardless of project size, so the project would become a carryover project requiring a borrowing vote.

budget_items.topic: Bond financing for a new source
budget_items.what_was_said: A new source would not get SRF funding, so would pay the full bond rate with no principal forgiveness.

decisions.decision: Once the SRF intended use plan is final, the district would send a letter to the SRF program describing the changed project scope and request.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners heard a consultant present a draft master plan recommending one combined PFAS treatment plant at Lancaster Avenue for the Lancaster and Hickory Hills wells.
The plan also calls for a separate treatment plant at Keating, estimated on its own.

The presenter described state revolving fund financing, with zero percent loans and possible principal forgiveness, and said first-year funding is capped, which would make this a carryover project needing a borrowing vote.
Once the state's intended use plan is final, the district would send the program a letter describing the changed project scope and request.
No votes were taken; the only motion was to adjourn, and no public comment was recorded.

why_it_matters: The plan points toward a large PFAS treatment build for the town's water supply, and its cost would reach water bills through borrowing; the amounts were stated aloud as estimates and are not confirmed figures.
Because first-year state funding is capped, residents should expect a borrowing vote, and a new water source would not qualify for state financing, so it would cost more to borrow for.
watch_next: The final state revolving fund intended use plan, followed by the district's letter describing the changed project scope.
A borrowing vote, which the presenter said would be required if the project becomes a carryover project.
